Extract 1-Row Causal Health Check from a TMLE Fit

Source: R/tidymodels_verbs.R
glance.tmle_fit.Rd

Summarizes sample sizes, cross-fitting metadata, targeting convergence (epsilon, mean_eif), plug-in vs. TMLE shift, propensity positivity bounds and truncation rate, Kish effective sample sizes (ess_treated, ess_control), maximum single-observation EIF leverage, and Super Learner nuisance performance.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tmle_fit'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted "tmle_fit" object.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A 1-row tibble::tibble().

Details

How to Read the Causal Health Check

  • mean_eif: The sample average of the Efficient Influence Function \(\frac{1}{n}\sum D_i^*\). A healthy TMLE solves the EIF score equation, so abs(mean_eif) must be near zero (< 1e-4).

  • epsilon: The magnitude of the targeting fluctuation step. Values close to 0 mean the initial ML outcome fit already had little residual confounding bias; larger magnitudes show how strongly TMLE adjusted the initial predictions to remove bias.

  • plugin_vs_tmle_shift: Difference between the final targeted TMLE ATE and the untargeted G-computation plug-in ATE. Quantifies the exact causal bias correction performed by the targeting step.

  • pct_truncated & ess_treated/ess_control: Share of propensity scores clipped to [g_bound_low, g_bound_high] and Kish's effective sample size under inverse-propensity weighting. High truncation (> 5%) or tiny ESS signals near-positivity violations (Petersen et al., 2012).

  • max_eif_leverage: Largest single observation's share of total EIF variance. Values > 0.10 flag an influential observation dominating the standard error.

References

Petersen, M. L., Porter, K. E., Gruber, S., Wang, Y., & van der Laan, M. J. (2012). Diagnosing and responding to violations in the positivity assumption. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 21(1), 31–54.

Schuler, M. S., & Rose, S. (2017). Targeted maximum likelihood estimation for causal inference in observational studies. American Journal of Epidemiology, 185(1), 65–73.
